findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`) the raw website URL is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, and `include_website_name?` only checks `website.present?`, so it is serialized for those users. It contains the host and, when the host matches the forum, the full path, so the restricted URL is effectively exposed again. This defeats the anti-spam restriction the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism exists to enforce. Fix: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list, or gate `include_website_name?` on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: Untrusted-attribute spec does not cover website_name
findings.body: The 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec checks that bio, location, website and profile/card background are not serialized. The new `website_name` attribute is not in this list, so the spec does not catch the leak where a TL0 user's website host and path are serialized to anonymous viewers. Add `website_name` to this list and make the untrusted check cover it.

findings.title: Trailing slash on same-domain website is shown as 'example.com/'
findings.body: For a website such as `http://example.com/` on a forum at `example.com`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so `website_name` becomes `"example.com/"`. Users who type a bare domain with a trailing slash will see a stray slash that the previous client-side `split('/')[2]` logic did not produce. Consider stripping a bare `/` path, for example by treating a path of `/` as empty.

findings.title: Domain comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. A website entered as `http://Example.com/user` on a forum at `example.com` fails the `==` test on line 141 and falls through to the else branch. The result is `Example.com` with no path, so the feature silently does not apply. Downcase both hosts before comparing, including in the `ends_with?` and sibling comparisons.

findings.title: Sibling-domain heuristic treats different registrable domains as the same site
findings.body: The branch on line 146 compares everything after the first label. For a forum at `y.co.uk` and a website at `x.co.uk/page`, both have three labels and the comparison yields `co.uk == co.uk`, so the full path is shown as if the website belonged to the forum's site. The heuristic does not account for public suffixes such as `co.uk` or `github.io`. The result is misleading display text for unrelated sites, not a security issue, but it does not match the stated intent of the feature.
